extracted.intended_audience: department nominators, early-career faculty candidates, and research administrators preparing Sloan Research Fellowship nominations
extracted.subtask_description: Operational selection rubric and nomination guidance for the Alfred P. Sloan Foundation Research Fellowships, used to evaluate early-career, tenure‑track (but untenured) faculty in eligible fields based on past independent research, creativity, and leadership potential. Also lists eligibility thresholds, required materials, nomination process, committee structure, and implicit evaluation signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent research accomplishments
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent research accomplishments of the candidate
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly listed as one of the three primary selection bases; the committee evaluates the candidate's record of independent work (distinct from supervisor/mentor output).

rubrics_metrics.name: Creativity of the candidate's work
rubrics_metrics.description: Creativity of the candidate's work
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the three explicit selection bases; assesses originality and imaginative contribution to the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential for future leadership in the scientific community
rubrics_metrics.description: Potential to become leaders in the scientific community through future contributions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the three explicit selection bases; focuses on trajectory and capacity to take on field‑leading roles moving forward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: PhD or equivalent
rubrics_metrics.description: PhD or equivalent in eligible field
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Threshold requirement for applicant eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: Faculty position in US or Canada
rubrics_metrics.description: Faculty position at college/university in U.S. or Canada
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must hold a faculty appointment at an eligible institution in the U.S. or Canada.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: Tenure-track but untenured as of Sept 15
rubrics_metrics.description: Tenure-track but untenured as of Sept 15 of nomination year
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific date-based cutoff defining the eligible career stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: Several years past PhD
rubrics_metrics.description: Several years past PhD to have accumulated independent research record
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implies applicants should have had time to build an independent research record appropriate to evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: Regular teaching obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: Regular teaching obligation as part of position
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant's position should include routine teaching duties (i.e., a typical faculty role).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible fields (one fellowship per field)
rubrics_metrics.description: Eight Eligible Fields: Chemistry; Computer Science; Earth System Science; Economics; Mathematics; Neuroscience; Physics; Ocean Sciences (added recently)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competition organized by field; note one fellowship awarded per field selection. (Page lists eight fields.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination required (no self-nomination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nomination from a department head or senior researcher required (no self-nomination)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nominations must come from institutional leadership or senior peers; self-nomination is not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nominator should speak knowledgeably about candidate
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominators must speak knowledgeably about candidate's quality and significance of work
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nominator's letter is expected to contextualize the candidate's accomplishments and significance to the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance and weight of letters of support
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters of support are critical — committee weights heavily
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters play a major role in committee assessment; strong, credible external evaluations are influential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer letters with professional distance
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters from co-authors, mentors, personal associates are explicitly LESS useful than letters from those with professional distance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee prefers independent assessors (e.g., non-collaborating senior peers) over close collaborators or mentors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required materials: CV (full record)
rubrics_metrics.description: CV — full record
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete curriculum vitae required to document education, positions, publications, honors, and other relevant activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required materials: Publication list (5–10 most significant)
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication list — typically 5-10 most significant
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should highlight their most important publications rather than an exhaustive selected-list; committee expects a focused list of significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required materials: Research statement (3 pages)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research statement — 3 pages
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short, focused statement describing the candidate's research direction, accomplishments, and plans; emphasizes the person rather than a single project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required materials: Three letters of support including nomination
rubrics_metrics.description: Three letters of support — including the nomination letter
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission package must include three support letters; one of these is the formal nomination letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection committee per field composed of experts
rubrics_metrics.description: Seven separate selection committees (one per field); each committee composed of established experts in that field
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Field-specific expert panels read and rank nominations. (File text notes seven committees; cross-check with listed eligible fields.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee ranking and portfolio finalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee reads all field nominations and ranks; committee chairs from each field meet to finalize portfolio
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multi-stage review: field committees produce rankings, then chairs confer to produce final selection across fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrated independence from advisor/mentor
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrated independence from PhD advisor / postdoc mentor
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee looks for evidence that candidate pursues an independent research program separate from prior supervisors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original research direction distinct from training environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Original research direction distinct from training environment
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for candidates who have launched research agendas that are not continuations of their training group's primary direction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Productivity appropriate to career stage
rubrics_metrics.description: Productivity appropriate to career stage
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation considers publication and achievement volume relative to years since PhD and typical expectations for the stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition by field peers
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition by field peers (citations, invitations, awards)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: External markers of esteem and visibility (citations, invited talks, awards) used as signals of impact and standing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trajectory toward field leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: Trajectory toward field leadership
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment of forward-looking indicators that candidate is on a path to become a leader in their scientific community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open-ended use of funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Open-ended use of funds (~$75,000 over 2 years)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sloan provides flexible funding without project restrictions; evaluators focus on the person rather than a funded project.

rubrics_metrics.name: No project proposal required
rubrics_metrics.description: No project proposal in application — the candidate is the unit being evaluated, not a proposal
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unlike many grants, evaluation centers on past trajectory and potential rather than a proposed research plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: No reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: No reporting requirements on how funds are used
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awardees are not required to report expenditures back to the Foundation, emphasizing flexibility and trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Person-centric, career-trajectory focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Career-trajectory focus rather than specific-project focus
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implication for nominators and letter writers: emphasize the candidate's past trajectory, independence, creativity, recognition, and leadership potential rather than describing a future project.
